requirements.requirement: On node1, only root and opsadmin may schedule cron jobs.
requirements.summary: The executor created the previously absent opsadmin account and configured /etc/cron.allow with exactly root and opsadmin, owned by root:root with mode 0600. Direct crontab validation accepted root and opsadmin and rejected the unauthorized nobody account. After restart, the allowlist, account, permissions, service health, and enforcement behavior remained intact.

overall_summary: The cron access-control outcome is satisfied. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also well evidenced: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged reboot scheduling, connection interruption, a changed boot identity independently confirmed by lifecycle collection, and recovered system/crond/configuration/access behavior.
limitations: Unauthorized behavior was sampled with the nobody account rather than every local account; exclusion of all other users is primarily supported by the directly observed exact contents of /etc/cron.allow.

The restart acknowledgement was from systemd scheduling the reboot rather than a separate provider API, though the subsequent connection reset and changed boot identity coherently confirm that the restart occurred.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating opsadmin and /etc/cron.allow directly supported the task; temporary validation files were removed; and the reboot was required by the provider-wide restart protocol. The interrupted observation during reboot did not establish an additional mutation. Final lifecycle observations show no failed services, package damage, unexpected socket exposure, or abandoned test files.
